chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Tadd Dameron's addiction, arrest and death
summary: Dameron lied about quitting, was busted by an undercover agent, then drank himself to death despite medical warnings.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: And like Tadd this is what killed Tadd, Tadd Dameron. Tadd and I were very dear friends, but Tadd would always lie to

me about it. He didn't want me to know because he knew how I felt about it. And he was -- oh, no, John, I've quit, you know, he would tell me this, and I knew that he hadn't quit. He wanted me to do a recording with John Simmons and Benny Golson and someone else. This was when I was with Nat Cole, and so I was going to -- I went to his -- and Shadow Wilson. Okay.

So I went by his house, he was going to tell me the tunes we were going to do, and in the meantime he told me, well I'm finished, I don't use any dope any more. So I went to his house to get the music, and while I was there in walked Shadow Wilson, who I knew was on it, in walked John Simmons who I knew was on it, and Philly Joe Jones. And he got up and went in the back with all of them, and the last time he came out I had got my guitar and left. You know.
They do hang out together, MS. WILLARD: (Inaudible).

Oh, but wait a minute. Right after that they busted him, because one of the guys who he was friendly with wasn't a musician, was the police, was an undercover agent, and he just let him stay out until he, you know, had Thanksgiving dinner with him one -- this time then busted him. You know, because he liked him. He just let him stay out a while and then he just busted him.
But now, Tad finally did quit, but it was too late. When he quit he started drinking, and the doctor advised him

not to drink. That he couldn't drink. But he used to drink himself to death. I would go to New York -- we were appearing at the Copa at the time, and I was living at the President Hotel, and I'd have whiskey in my room, you know, but I may take a drink once a month you know. Whiskey wasn't my thing. As a matter of fact -- I could drink, I like to drink, but and work, I never could drink and work. So when I got off from work usually it's too late to drink then, so I just let it sit there.

So any way, Tad would come by to see me, and would drink a whole fifth, you know. And I'd tell him, come on, Tad, and he'd say, no, he'd drink it all. So this is really what finally got him and he stayed in the hospital. So I moved to Los Angeles, and I -- one morning I get this call and it was Tad, and he asked me to put my wife on the extension, and just listen, and he played for us for about a half hour. He just played, from New York. Just played. And right after that he died. But we were very dear friends.
